entries.root_cause: Two coupled process defects: (1) CI triage did not descend workflow -> failed job -> job logs before declaring evidence unavailable; (2) narrow routing tests used a partial reviewed-authority fixture and mocked only the exporter consumer, so a newly added independent validator consumed the same marker and changed the fixture's meaning.
entries.verification: On exact head b756fdb387d35237ba711aafeecd0528cd22df88, CI and Windows Desktop are GREEN; only Control Plane failed because this regression-memory entry violated its schema. The routing-test fixture repair itself passed the full product test suite.
entries.residual_risk: Future validators may consume shared partial-authority fixtures in unrelated unit tests unless those tests explicitly declare/stub non-owned consumers.
entries.prevention_rule: For FAILED CI, always fetch actual failed job logs when the connector exposes them. For partial/mock authority fixtures, identify every consumer introduced by the change and either construct complete authority or explicitly isolate unrelated consumers; never weaken production validation to satisfy a narrow unit test.
entries.symptom: PR #556 remained red across repeated runs because orchestration stopped at workflow/job failure summaries instead of retrieving the available job logs; once logs were inspected, three reviewed-export routing tests were shown to use intentionally partial promotion-marker fixtures that the new EOF note-gap validator correctly rejected as invalid production authority.
entries.fix: Retrieve failed job logs before any opaque-blocker classification. Keep production fail-closed behavior intact. In tests intentionally using partial authority fixtures, explicitly stub unrelated authority consumers so the test remains scoped to its owned behavior.

entries.root_cause: Feature-file creation was attempted before the intended feature branch had been successfully created, causing disposable placeholder files to be written to the default branch. Repeated write attempts compounded commit-history noise even though each placeholder was immediately removed and no product logic remained on main.
entries.verification: Every accidental placeholder file was deleted from main before feature implementation continued. The real feature branch was then created explicitly with the branch-creation operation, and subsequent feature writes targeted only orchestrator/eof-beat-phase-solver.
entries.residual_risk: The add/delete cleanup commits remain as harmless default-branch history noise because rewriting main would be destructive and is not justified.
entries.prevention_rule: Before any feature file create/update/delete, first create or resolve the intended non-default branch and verify that branch creation succeeded. Never use a contents write as a branch-existence probe, and never fall back to the default branch when a requested feature branch is missing.
entries.symptom: Temporary placeholder files briefly appeared on main while starting the #455 beat-phase implementation, despite the change being intended for a gated feature branch.
entries.fix: Removed each placeholder immediately, stopped feature writes, created orchestrator/eof-beat-phase-solver explicitly from main, and resumed implementation only after branch creation succeeded.
